title: "anchors freeze"

---

<!-- cli-reference:start — generated by `go run ./tools/sitecli` from the CLI; edit the command's help in the code, not this block -->

Freeze the project, or a part of it, until `anchors thaw`.

```text
With a scope, keeps a PART of the project as it is, by decision, until someone thaws it:

  anchors freeze --reason "the plan mode ships next quarter" --unit PAWAP --rule CARTU-B02 --file src/flags.ts
  anchors freeze QLDTQ-F01 --unit HOMEH     add a scope to a recorded freeze
  anchors freeze show [QLDTQ-F01]           the freezes, or every place one covers

The freeze is recorded once, with its reason, in the project's doctrine document (--in when
it has several), coded with the letter F; each place carries a mark with the code. With no
doctrine, the marks carry the reason. A frozen part answers "frozen" in every gate, leaves the
reports and the runs, and warns whoever reaches it — it never blocks.

With no scope and no code, stops the work on the entire project, in three layers.

  1. writes 'enabled: false' and the reason into anchors.yaml, and PUSHES
  2. creates a ruleset on the remote that blocks push and merge on every branch
  3. opens an issue with the reason, so whoever hits the brake knows what happened

The --reason is MANDATORY. A freeze with no written reason is indistinguishable from
broken configuration, and whoever hits it tries to work around it instead of reading.

The commit and the push are made with --no-verify, on purpose: the hooks that this
command has just activated would refuse the freeze itself.

WHOEVER FIXES IT PASSES. The admin bypasses the ruleset, and '--no-verify' bypasses the
hooks — the brake exists to stop work by INERTIA, not the fix that
releases it.
```

## Uso

```bash
anchors freeze [freeze code] [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Padrão | O que faz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--file` |  | freeze one file, by its path (repeatable) |
| `--in` |  | the doctrine document that records the freeze, when the project has several |
| `--no-push` |  | do not commit or push anchors.yaml |
| `--no-ruleset` |  | do not create the ruleset on the remote (only the local brake) |
| `--reason` |  | why the project is being frozen (required) |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |
| `--rule` |  | freeze one rule, by its code (repeatable) |
| `--unit` |  | freeze a whole unit, by its code (repeatable) |

## Subcomandos

### `anchors freeze show`

List the freezes, or every place one covers.

#### Uso

```bash
anchors freeze show [freeze code] [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Padrão | O que faz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

## Congelar o projeto — família

Comandos da mesma família — o que distingue cada um:

| Comando | O que faz |
| --- | --- |
| **`anchors freeze`** | Freeze the project, or a part of it, until `anchors thaw` |
| [`anchors thaw`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/thaw/) | Thaw the project, or a frozen part of it |

Quando o projeto atinge uma release candidate ou marco de entrega, é necessário impedir modificações acidentais, mantendo apenas comandos de inspeção e auditoria liberados.

---

## 1. Congelando o Projeto (`anchors freeze`)

```bash
# Congela o projeto com justificativa de auditoria
anchors freeze --reason="Validação da Release Candidate v2.0.0"
```

Quando congelado:
- Comandos de escrita e mutação (`new`, `work`, `deliver`, `map build`) são **bloqueados**.
- Comandos somente-leitura (`status`, `doctor`, `guide`, `coverage`, `version`) **continuam funcionando**.

---

## 2. Descongelando (`anchors thaw`)

```bash
anchors thaw
```

Retoma as atividades normais de desenvolvimento e desbloqueia a fila de tarefas.
